summary: Preview of Argentina's home CONMEBOL 2026 World Cup qualifier against Paraguay at Estadio Monumental on Thursday, October 12, 2023. It covers Lionel Messi's fitness (on the bench, expected to play most of the second half), injuries and lineups for both teams, new Paraguay coach Daniel Garnero's debut, and broadcast and streaming options by territory plus kickoff times.
one_line: Preview of Argentina vs Paraguay 2026 World Cup qualifier on Oct. 12, 2023, covering lineups, Messi's fitness, TV and streaming options, and kickoff times.
key_facts: Argentina host Paraguay in a CONMEBOL 2026 World Cup qualifier at Estadio Monumental, kicking off Thursday, October 12 at 8 p.m. local time in Buenos Aires.
The match kicks off at 7 p.m. ET and 4 p.m. PT in the USA/Canada, and at 12 a.m. BST on Fri, Oct. 13 in the UK.
Lionel Messi is not starting but is likely to play much or all of the second half; he missed the Bolivia match and four Inter Miami games after it.
Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni named a 36-man squad; Angel Di Maria, Paulo Dybala and Juan Foyth withdrew injured, and Lisandro Martinez is out after another foot operation.
Julian Alvarez and Alejandro Garnacho are considered the future of Argentina's forward line.
Argentina's starting lineup is a 4-3-3 with E. Martinez in goal and Nicolas Tagliafico keeping his left-back spot ahead of the returning Marcos Acuna.
Daniel Garnero makes his debut as Paraguay head coach and made five changes after the loss to Venezuela, swapping out the entire midfield.
Adam Bareiro replaces Gabriel Avalos at striker and earns his debut international cap.
Paraguay have not reached a FIFA tournament since 2010 but see the expanded 2026 field as a real chance to qualify.
Miguel Almiron is Paraguay's top scoring threat, with three goals in his past five matches for Newcastle United.
Carlos Coronel of the New York Red Bulls starts in goal for Paraguay after earning his first two caps in September; Antony Silva has been phased out.
In the USA, rights for Argentina's home qualifiers went to Telemundo and Univision, so the match airs on Universo and streams on Fubo and Telemundo/Universo services.
The match is not broadcast in Australia, Canada and the UK because CONMEBOL has not sold rights there, but it is on FIFA+ for free in select territories.
